Agoda 2027 Asia Travel Pulse: 53% of Asian travelers plan with AI but 89% want the final say on hotel bookings
Digital travel platform Agoda launches its 2027 Asia Travel Pulse and reveals that more than half (53%) of surveyed Asian travelers now use AI to plan their trips, up from 33% last year. The biggest increases were in Vietnam and Taiwan.
Despite the reported increase in AI usage, most travelers still prefer to make the actual booking themselves. Of those surveyed, 57% would rather book a hotel on their own, and a further 32% would only let an AI agent book with conditions attached. In total, 89% want to keep some control over the booking, compared to 6% who would completely trust an AI agent to book for them.

The most common uses are building an itinerary (64%), getting travel inspiration (45%) and comparing hotels or flights (44%), while 7% would use AI to make a booking. Travelers in Taiwan (75%) and South Korea (73%) are the most likely to use AI to build an itinerary. AI use for travel planning more than doubled in Vietnam, from 30% to 63%, and nearly doubled in Taiwan, from 35% to 63%, the largest increases in the region.
